nodes.title: Note: MiniMax H3
widgets_values:
## MiniMax H3

[MiniMax H3](https://www.minimax.io/blog/minimax-h3) is MiniMax's general-purpose, omni-modal generation model. It jointly understands text, image, video, and audio, and generates video with **native stereo audio**: voice, sound effects, and music are modeled jointly in a single forward pass, not layered on afterward. Output is up to 2K resolution, 24fps, and up to about 15 seconds.

## ComfyUI links
- [ComfyUI#15224](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/15224)
- [🤗 Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3)

## About this workflow

This template runs the **reference-to-video (ref2va)** task using the `MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo` node. It takes any mix of reference images, videos, and standalone audio, and weaves them into the generation to lock in a character's identity, a style, a motion, a camera move, or a voice.

**Key inputs**

- **ref_images / ref_videos / ref_video_audios / ref_audios**: up to 9 reference images, 3 reference videos (each may carry its own paired soundtrack), and 3 standalone reference audio clips
- **prompt**: reference the inputs by tag, in the exact order they were connected, for example `<Picture 1>`, `<Video 1>`, `<Audio 1>`, then describe the target scene, motion, and audio
- **ref_image_size**: `match` scales references down to the generation's resolution (faster); `max` keeps up to a 2048px short edge for stronger identity fidelity, at the cost of speed since reference tokens ride along every sampling step
- **width / height**: set via Resolution Selector.
- **duration (seconds)**: converted to a valid frame `length` by the Math Expression node

**Sampling and decode**

- Sampler: `res_multistep`. `beta` or `normal` scheduler tends to outperform `simple` for reference-heavy prompts like this one
- The sampler's joint audio+video `LATENT` output feeds directly into both `VAEDecode` (video, `minimax_h3_video_vae_fp16`) and `VAEDecodeAudio` (audio, `minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32`); each decode node automatically pulls its own half out of the packed latent. `CreateVideo` then muxes the two into a single MP4 with synced sound
- The diffusion model here is `minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors`, a different set of weights from the `fl2va` model used by the t2v/i2v templates

Ref2va's output is very sensitive to prompt wording; matching the reference tags precisely and being explicit about which reference drives which part of the shot tends to work best.

subject_definitions:
@image1 is the VX-07 ARES armour.
@image2 is Marcus.
@image3 gives the architecture, wet asphalt, overcast rain light and parked traffic only; its calmly walking pedestrians and moving traffic are replaced by the panicking crowd and abandoned cars described below.
@image4 is the monster, standing three times Marcus's height. The smaller figure beside it in that reference is a scale comparison only and does not appear in the video.

summary:
[reference generation] @image2 armours up, takes a thrown car head-on, punches @image4 and sends it down the street.

detailed_description:
Blockbuster superhero film, photoreal, overcast rain, wet asphalt, deep street perspective under the elevated track of @image3. Every pedestrian runs away from the fight for the whole video; nobody walks, nobody watches calmly.

[Shot 1] Close-up on @image2 in the flooded street in his tuxedo. Plates of @image1 come in fast from off frame and build onto him, running continuously across the whole shot, never rushing and never springing back: every piece travels inward and seats with weight, cyan seams lighting as each lock closes. Nothing detaches or floats free. People stream past behind him, running the other way. His lips stay pressed closed and he does not speak at any point in the video.

[Shot 2] At 00:03.500, cut low and wide as @image4 tears an empty parked taxi off the road and hurls it down the lane, the car turning end over end. The camera Trucks backwards with large amplitude at fast speed.

[Shot 3] At 00:06.000, cut to a low side-on shot: @image2 stands right of frame in profile, visor, chest plate and crossed forearms square to screen-left in every frame. The taxi enters from the left edge intact and filling the frame, slams into his forearms and stops dead, crumpling around them while he is driven backwards through the water, heels gouging two long trenches before he plants. The wreck then breaks apart off his front and drops.

[Shot 4] At 00:09.000, cut in tight past @image4's shoulder onto @image2. He drops his shoulder and drives his fist across the frame into the chest plate of @image4, and the fist stays buried there for the rest of the shot, forearm plates compressing, @image4's chest caving around it. @image4 stays on its feet and in place throughout this shot; nothing leaves the ground yet. The camera is Static.

[Shot 5] At 00:10.600, cut wide down the street as @image4 flies ten metres backwards through the air, lands hard and skids through the water. A low sheet of white spray rolls outward along the street with it, hiding the parked cars as it passes. The camera is Static. Both helmets stay sealed and neither character speaks.

overall_soundscape:
Hard rain on metal and asphalt and an elevated train rumbling overhead through the whole video. Running footsteps splashing away and a distant wordless crowd cry, never fully stopping. Tearing sheet metal and a long rising whoosh as the car comes down the lane, then one huge dull impact of mass on mass, metal buckling, heels grinding through grit, glass cascading off him. The punch is one enormous low boom with a hard metallic crack inside it and a half-second of near-silence behind it, then the rip of spray, a heavy body hitting water and sliding, car alarms down the block and armour ticking and draining. Nobody in the video speaks any words.

non_diegetic_music:
Low taiko building under the armour build. Distorted low brass enters on the throw and drops out completely half a beat before the fist lands, then one sustained chord over the landing with the drums returning underneath.

subject_definitions:
@image1 is the yellow robot.
@image2 is the yellow car. Use its shape, paint and black stripes only; the studio backdrop and the multiple views in that sheet are a reference layout and do not appear in the video.
@image3 is the abandoned brick factory yard, and gives the architecture, the gantry crane, the scrap piles, the dirt ground and the low sunset light.
@image4 is the grey monster, standing a head taller than @image1. The smaller figure beside it in that reference is a scale comparison only and does not appear in the video.
@image1 and @image2 are the same character in two forms, never two separate things in frame.

summary:
[reference generation] @image2 slides into the yard, transforms into @image1, trades blows with @image4 and rockets it.

detailed_description:
Blockbuster action film in the style of a live-action Transformers movie, photoreal, handheld shoulder-mounted camera with constant human float in every shot, low sunset light, dust hanging across the yard of @image3.

[Shot 1] Wide low angle across the dirt. @image2 comes in fast from the left edge, brakes hard and slides broadside toward the lens, rear wheels spinning, throwing a sheet of dust that rolls outward across the yard and keeps travelling rather than settling.

[Shot 2] At 00:02.600, cut closer as @image2 transforms into @image1 epic transformers movies like, every parts moves, rotates, folds, and roll. nothing left on the ground
[Shot 3] At 00:07.000, cut tight and low as @image4 charges in from screen-right and swings. @image1 blocks it on a forearm, drives a fist into the chest of @image4, then takes a backhand that snaps its head aside and puts it back two steps through the dirt. The camera is Static.

[Shot 4] At 00:09.000, cut in close on the right forearm of @image1. Plates on the forearm hinge outward and lock open, a rocket pod rotates up out of the housing on a pivot arm and seats hard, its tube aligning forward. The camera is Static.

[Shot 5] At 00:11.300, cut behind @image1 with its right arm held out large in the foreground on the left of frame, the open pod on that forearm sharp and in shot throughout, @image4 downrange. The rocket leaves that tube in frame with a hard backblast off the pod, crosses the yard on a corkscrewing smoke trail and strikes @image4 in the chest. A fireball climbs and rolls outward, throwing burning scrap, a wall of dust racing ahead of it along the ground. Bricks come down off the factory wall and stay down. Neither character speaks at any point in the video.

overall_soundscape:
Wind across an empty yard and loose metal ticking. A hard engine howl and a long gravel skid on the arrival. The transform starts as a fine dense rustle of hundreds of small plates and ratcheting gears, then deepens into heavy hydraulics and big panels seating, ending with two feet planting in dirt. Charging footfalls, a heavy forearm block, one impact boom with a metallic crack, a flat cracking backhand and boots dragging through grit. Plates hinging open and a pod locking into place. Rocket ignition and a hiss across the yard, a low detonation with a deep sub thud under it, burning scrap raining down, fire roaring, bricks collapsing. No voices anywhere in the video.

non_diegetic_music:
Low brass swell under the arrival. Percussion builds through the transform and drops out completely as the backhand lands, leaving the pod deployment almost bare. One full orchestral hit on the detonation, then a slow sustained chord over the fire.

detailed_description:
Blockbuster action film in the style of a live-action Transformers movie, photoreal, handheld shoulder-mounted camera with constant human float in every shot, low sunset light, smoke and ash drifting across the yard of @image3.

[Shot 1] Continuing unbroken. For the first second nothing changes: @image1 stands left of frame with the rocket pod still open on its right forearm, thin smoke curling from the tube, the fireball downrange burning down into a low wall of flame, the camera barely settling. Then @image4 walks straight out of the fire toward the camera, burning scrap sliding off its shoulders, orange seams brighter than before, not one plate broken. It stops, tilts its head at @image1, and rolls its shoulders once. The camera pushes slowly toward it at slow speed.

[Shot 2] At 00:05.000, cut low and behind @image4 as it drops into a sprint at @image1, feet cracking the concrete, dust ripping backwards past the lens. @image1 snaps the pod shut, the plates folding back flat into the forearm, and sets its feet. The camera Trucks with large amplitude at fast speed, holding level with @image4's hip.

[Shot 3] At 00:08.200, cut tight and static. @image4 drives a fist up under the chest plate of @image1. The fist stays buried there, the plate folding inward around it and splitting along its own panel seams, one shoulder pauldron tearing loose and hanging by its cabling. @image1 is lifted off its heels. @image4 stays planted and in place throughout this shot. The camera is Static.

[Shot 4] At 00:11.000, cut wide as @image1 flies backwards into the brick wall of @image3 and goes through it. The wall caves in a spreading crack and collapses over it, bricks and window frames coming down in a slab, a dust cloud rolling out along the ground and hiding the scrap piles as it passes. The gantry crane above sags and drops one end.

[Shot 5] At 00:13.400, cut in close as @image1 pushes up out of the rubble on one arm, torn chest venting blue arcs that spit across the broken plating, the loose pauldron dragging. Behind it @image4 walks in through the dust, unhurried. Neither character speaks at any point in the video.

subject_definitions:
@image1 is the first frame: the troll in the forest clearing with the moth at his raised hand.

summary:
[first-last frame] The troll watches the moth settle on his finger, softens, then loses it.

detailed_description:
Photoreal fantasy cinema, shallow depth of field, soft shafts of light through the canopy. One continuous shot, no cuts, no camera moves beyond a slow push toward his face.

The moth flutters in a tight irregular loop and settles on his outstretched finger. He goes completely still the instant it touches him, holding the hand frozen so as not to startle it, only his eyes moving.

His face works through it slowly and in order: first the wary tension he starts with, brow low; then the brow lifting as it lands, eyes widening a fraction; then the corners of his mouth pulling back into a small closed-lip smile, tusks catching the light, deep creases forming around his eyes. He breathes out through his nose, chest dropping.

The moth lifts off and drifts up out of frame. His hand stays exactly where it is for a long beat, fingers still curled. The smile fades, the brow settles, and his eyes follow it up and stay there after it has gone.

His lips stay closed and he does not speak at any point in the video. Ferns and flowers move faintly in the air the whole time.

overall_soundscape:
Deep forest room tone, wood pigeons somewhere far off, leaves and ferns shifting. Papery moth wings close to the lens as it circles and settles. One long slow breath out through the nose, and a low involuntary rumble in his chest, wordless. Everything drops back as it lifts away, leaving the canopy and one distant bird. No voices anywhere in the video.

non_diegetic_music:
A single sustained high string, almost inaudible, entering as the moth lands. One low cello note under the breath. It thins to nothing as the moth leaves, and does not resolve.

subject_definitions:
@image1 is Vane.

summary:
[reference generation] Vane launches off a rooftop and swings across a city canyon in three shots, ending coming straight at the lens.

detailed_description:
Blockbuster superhero film, photoreal, anamorphic, golden-hour haze over a dense modern city of glass and stone towers.

[Shot 1] Vane crouches on the parapet of the tallest tower with the skyline far below him, wind dragging at the fabric across his shoulders, then pushes off and drops head-first down the face of the building. The camera Pedestals down with him with large amplitude at fast speed, glass panels streaking past.

[Shot 2] At 00:04.000, cut to a tracking shot running level beside Vane mid-arc between two towers, a thin grey cable line taut from his fist to an anchor above and ahead of him. The swing runs continuously across the rest of the video, never rushing and never springing back: he releases at the top of each arc, falls free through the gap, fires again and is pulled up into the next, three arcs deep through the canyon. Two rules hold in every frame: the line is always taut and always anchored ahead of him, and the city slides past faster than he falls. The camera Tracks with him with large amplitude at fast speed. Pigeons scatter off a ledge and a loose banner snaps in the draft as he passes.

[Shot 3] At 00:08.500, cut to a low static angle from the street canyon looking straight up between the towers. Vane swings in from the far distance and comes at the lens, growing until he fills the frame and crosses over it. The camera never moves; the scale comes from him arriving. He is masked throughout and does not speak at any point in the video.

overall_soundscape:
Constant high wind across the towers, fabric snapping and rippling, and the long hiss of a body cutting air on the drops. Each arc carries a sharp cable whip, a metal bite as the anchor sets, then a deep rope creak under load. Underneath, thin street traffic and horns far below, pigeon wings clattering off stone, and a last heavy rush of air past the lens as he crosses frame. No voices anywhere in the video.

non_diegetic_music:
Full orchestra. Low strings ostinato under the rooftop, snare and taiko entering on the drop, brass building through the swings in rising three-note figures. It peaks on the final approach and cuts off hard as he crosses the lens.

subject_definitions:
@image1 is Kira, the armoured soldier, and Bhodi, the armoured silverback beside her; it also gives the ruined city, the burnt vehicles, the white overcast sky and the dust-grey light.

summary:
[reference generation] Kira speaks to Bhodi in the rubble, he answers without words, and they rise together and turn toward the smoke.

detailed_description:
Photoreal blockbuster war epic, overcast white sky, anamorphic, desaturated dust and ash grade.

[Shot 1] Kira kneels against Bhodi's chest in the rubble field, her rifle lowered with the muzzle resting on broken concrete and her finger off the trigger. She stares out past the lens, jaw clenched and eyes wet, then her face breaks open as she turns her head up toward him. Kira (S1), quiet and unsteady, says in English: "They're not coming back for us." Her lips close immediately after the final word and stay closed for the rest of the shot. The camera Arcs around the pair with small amplitude at slow speed.

[Shot 2] At 00:05.000, cut to a tight low angle on Bhodi's face. His eyes drop to her, the heavy brow creasing and the skin around his eyes tightening, and he lets out one long slow breath that moves his whole chest, then rests a huge hand flat across her back. His mouth stays closed through this entire shot and he does not speak at any point in the video; Kira sits soft out of focus at the frame edge with her lips closed. The camera Pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed.

[Shot 3] At 00:08.500, cut to behind them as both rise together and turn toward a black smoke column on the far skyline. Kira shoulders the rifle, her face hardening into dry-eyed set resolve. Kira (S1), flat and certain, says in English: "Then we go alone." Her lips close on the last word and stay closed. The camera Pedestals up with large amplitude at slow speed, opening the ruined city out behind them.

overall_soundscape:
Steady wind dragging across open rubble, loose grit sliding underfoot, and fires crackling somewhere off frame. Bhodi's slow heavy breathing through the nose runs under the whole video, with a deep chest rumble on the exhale. Armour plates knock and creak as they shift, a sling buckle rattles, and the rifle clicks onto her shoulder near the end, over distant masonry collapsing far away. No other voices anywhere in the video.

non_diegetic_music:
Solo cello holding one long low note under the opening. A low male choir hum enters on the exhale. Slow timpani pulse and rising strings build through the final turn and hold one chord to the end.

subject_definitions:
@image1 is the Vessel, and gives the void, the drifting coloured dust and the violet-and-gold palette.

summary:
